skill.name: next
skill.description: Next.js renderer for json-render that turns JSON specs into full Next.js applications with routes, layouts, SSR, and metadata. Use when working with @json-render/next, building Next.js apps from JSON specs, or creating AI-generated multi-page applications.
skill.summary: Guide AI assistants in building Next.js applications from JSON specs with routes, shared layouts, server rendering, and metadata.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: All 40 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline code formatting, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The source documents routine dependency installation and Next.js integration examples. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious data transfer; dependency implementations were not included in this review.

Layouts wrap page content. Every layout MUST include a `Slot` component where page content will be r

- **pushState**: Append to array. Params: `{ statePath, value, clearStatePath? }`
- **removeState**: Remove from array by index. Params: `{ statePath, index }`
Pages are server-rendered automatically. The `createNextApp` `Page` component is an async Server Com
- `schema` -- Custom schema for Next.js apps (for AI catalog generation)
- `matchRoute(spec, pathname)` -- Match a URL to a route spec
- `resolveMetadata(spec, route)` -- Resolve metadata for a route
- `slugToPath(slug)` -- Convert catch-all slug array to pathname

- `NextAppProvider` -- Context provider for registry and handlers
- `PageRenderer` -- Renders a page spec with optional layout

content.user_title: Build Next.js Apps from JSON Specifications
content.value_statement: Connecting JSON specifications to Next.js routes, layouts, and server rendering requires several integration steps. This skill guides AI assistants through the documented json-render setup.
actual_capabilities: Guide creation of NextAppSpec definitions with metadata, shared layouts, route definitions, and initial state.
Explain static, dynamic, catch-all, and optional catch-all route patterns.
Show createNextApp integration with Page, generateMetadata, and generateStaticParams exports.
Demonstrate NextAppProvider wiring for a component registry and action handlers.
Explain asynchronous server loaders and how their results become page initial state.
Document built-in navigation, state actions, and loading, error, and not-found components.
limitations: Contains guidance and examples, not a bundled application or renderer implementation.
Requires a Next.js project and separately installed json-render packages.
Does not provide the component registry, custom handlers, or database implementation referenced by its examples.
Does not include automated tests, deployment instructions, or authentication and authorization guidance.

use_cases.title: Connect a JSON-driven frontend
use_cases.description: Build shared layouts and route definitions, then connect the specification to Next.js page exports and a component registry.

use_cases.title: Prototype multiple application pages
use_cases.description: Translate a small application outline into JSON specifications with consistent navigation, page metadata, and shared layouts.

use_cases.title: Integrate server-loaded page data
use_cases.description: Plan asynchronous loaders, route matching, server rendering, and client hydration for pages backed by existing data services.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the minimum setup for using @json-render/next in my existing Next.js project. Identify required packages and missing application components.

prompt_templates.title: Define a two-page specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a NextAppSpec for home and about pages using my existing registry. Include shared navigation, a layout Slot, and page metadata.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: define routes and reusable layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Connect server rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate my specification with createNextApp and NextAppProvider. Show the catch-all route exports and identify any missing registry or handler definitions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: connect server and client entry points.

prompt_templates.title: Review a dynamic content integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my dynamic blog specification and server loader design. Check route patterns, metadata, static parameters, and layout Slots. Identify sensitive fields before client hydration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review data loading and rendering boundaries.

output_examples.input: Outline a home and about application with a shared layout.
output: The specification defines home and about routes with separate page titles.
Both routes reference one layout containing navigation and a Slot for page content.
The component registry must supply the custom components used by the specification.

output_examples.input: Explain how a dynamic blog page loads data before rendering.
output: The dynamic route uses a slug segment to identify the requested page.
An asynchronous server loader retrieves the post and returns page state.
The server component runs loaders and generates metadata before passing the resolved specification to the client renderer.
The application must implement its data access function and choose which fields may reach the client.

best_practices: Include a Slot in every shared layout and verify that referenced components exist in your registry.
Keep server utilities and client components in their documented entry points.
Review loader return values for sensitive data before they become page state, and test dynamic routes in your application.
anti_patterns: Copying examples without implementing the referenced registry, handlers, and data access functions.
Defining shared layouts without a Slot for page content.
Assuming server-loaded data remains private after it is passed to the client renderer.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and examples for integrating @json-render/next with a Next.js application. It does not bundle the renderer or a complete project.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What dependencies are required?
faq.answer: The quick start installs @json-render/core, @json-render/react, and @json-render/next. You also need a Next.js project and your application components.

faq.question: Does it cover dynamic routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents static paths, dynamic segments, catch-all segments, and optional catch-all segments using Next.js route conventions.

faq.question: How does server rendering work?
faq.answer: The documented Page component matches routes, runs server loaders, generates metadata, and passes the resolved specification to the client renderer for hydration.

faq.question: Why is page content missing from my layout?
faq.answer: Check that the layout includes a Slot component. Also verify that the route references the intended layout and the registry supplies its custom components.
